skill.name: openapi-to-typescript
skill.description: Converts OpenAPI 3.0 JSON or YAML specifications into TypeScript interfaces, request and response types, and runtime type guards.
skill.summary: Generate TypeScript interfaces and type guards from OpenAPI 3.0 specifications.
skill.author: softaworks

The system reconnaissance alerts matched type-checking examples and OpenAPI validation text, and no prompt-injection or exfiltration intent was found.

content.value_statement: API teams need TypeScript models that stay aligned with OpenAPI contracts. This skill converts OpenAPI 3.0 specs into interfaces, endpoint types, and runtime guards.
actual_capabilities: Validates required OpenAPI 3.0 fields before generation.
Maps primitive, formatted, array, enum, union, and intersection schemas to TypeScript types.
Generates interfaces from components/schemas with required and optional fields.
Creates request and response types from documented API paths.
Generates runtime type guards and a shared API error type.
limitations: Supports OpenAPI 3.0.x, not Swagger 2.0 or OpenAPI 3.1.
Uses referenced schema names directly instead of fully inlining every $ref.
Complex allOf and circular reference cases may need manual review.
Generates types and guards, not a full API client implementation.

use_cases.title: Frontend API Integration
use_cases.description: Convert backend OpenAPI specs into TypeScript contracts for UI data fetching and response handling.

use_cases.title: Shared Service Contracts
use_cases.description: Publish generated request and response types for teams that consume internal APIs.

use_cases.title: Response Validation in Tests
use_cases.description: Use generated type guards to validate API responses in automated test workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Basic Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate TypeScript interfaces from ./openapi.json and save them to types/api.ts. Report validation errors before writing files.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Custom Output Path
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert ./specs/service.yaml into TypeScript request, response, and schema types. Save the result to src/generated/api-types.ts.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Regenerated Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Regenerate types from ./openapi.yaml, compare the result with src/types/api.ts, and summarize any breaking type changes.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Complex Schemas
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert ./api/openapi.yaml and review oneOf, allOf, enums, arrays, and unresolved references. Flag areas needing manual review.

output_examples.input: An OpenAPI 3.0 product catalog spec with Product and Order schemas.
output_examples.output: A TypeScript file containing Product and Order interfaces, endpoint request and response types, type guards, and an API error type.

output_examples.input: A service spec with enum fields, arrays, and path parameters.
output_examples.output: Generated union types for enums, array property types, path request types, and warnings for unsupported schema references.

output_examples.input: An invalid OpenAPI document missing the paths section.
output_examples.output: A validation message explaining the missing paths field, with no generated output file.

best_practices: Validate the OpenAPI spec before generation to fix contract errors early.
Regenerate types whenever the source API specification changes.
Review warnings for unknown types, circular references, and complex allOf schemas.
anti_patterns: Do not edit generated files manually when the source spec can be updated.
Do not treat generated type guards as complete business-rule validation.
Do not ignore unresolved references or unknown types in generated output.

faq.question: Which OpenAPI versions are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports OpenAPI 3.0.x. It does not document support for Swagger 2.0 or OpenAPI 3.1.

faq.question: Does it generate a full API client?
faq.answer: No. It generates interfaces, endpoint types, type guards, and a shared API error type.

faq.question: Can it read YAML and JSON specs?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documentation states that JSON and YAML OpenAPI files are accepted.

faq.question: How are enums handled?
faq.answer: String enums are converted to TypeScript union types that represent the allowed literal choices.

faq.question: What happens when the spec is invalid?
faq.answer: The skill reports the validation error and stops before generating output.

faq.question: Can I choose the output file?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks where to save the generated TypeScript and uses types/api.ts as the default.
